## Example 3.7 · Set up the spreadsheet {#l2-example-3-7-setup .compact}

**Part 1: Setting up the data**

a) Open a new Google Sheet or Excel workbook.
b) Create three headers: **Score (x)**, **Frequency (Bar)**, **Frequency (Line)**.
c) Enter scores **1, 2, 3, 4, 5** and frequencies **4, 8, 12, 6, 2**.
d) Copy the same frequencies into the **Frequency (Line)** column.
e) Calculate the total frequency below the data.
f) Add **Relative Freq (Bar)** and **Relative Freq (Line)** columns.
g) Divide each frequency by the total; fill both new columns. Use an absolute reference such as `$B$7` for the total.
<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 43 · Example 3.7 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
With headers in row1 and data rows2–6, B7=SUM(B2:B6)=32; C2=B2, fill down; D2=B2/$B$7; E2=D2, fill down. Use the original frequency columns and two identical relative-frequency columns. These are the complete Part1 instructions, condensed only in wording.
:::
